item.title: Moving to a New Flat
item.description: Learn words and phrases for packing up a household, moving furniture and boxes, and getting settled in a new flat.

children.definition: A cardboard box used to hold or transport things.
children.example: We put the towels in a large carton so we could find them on our first night in the new flat.

children.definition: A sheet of plastic with small pockets of air that keep objects from getting damaged.
children.example: We covered each mirror with bubble wrap before putting it in the van.
collocations: wrap a mirror in bubble wrap

children.definition: A wide, strong strip of sticky material used to keep boxes closed.
children.example: I used two strips of packing tape across the bottom of each carton before filling it.
collocations: seal a carton with packing tape

children.definition: To close a box or package securely with tape or another sticky material.
children.example: Please seal the last carton with tape once the towels are inside.

children.definition: To take something apart into separate pieces.
children.example: We had to dismantle the wardrobe because it was too wide to go down the stairs.

children.definition: A complete list of the things in a place or the things being moved.
children.example: We made an inventory of the furniture and numbered cartons before the van left.

children.definition: A vehicle used to take furniture and other belongings from one home to another.
children.example: The moving van was big enough to take all our furniture in one trip.

children.definition: A small piece of equipment with wheels that you push or pull to move heavy things.
children.example: We used a trolley to move the heaviest cartons from the van to the lift.

children.definition: An area beside a building where vehicles stop so goods can be put in or taken out.
children.example: The van stopped in the loading bay behind the new building, next to the service lift.

children.definition: To take goods or belongings out of a vehicle.
children.example: We had twenty minutes to unload the van before the next household needed the space.

children.definition: To put things one on top of another.
children.example: Let's stack the cartons of towels by the wall so there is room to bring in the furniture.

children.definition: To start living in a new home.
children.example: We can move in on Friday and spend our first night in the new flat that evening.

children.definition: To put something back together after it has been taken apart.
children.example: We need to reassemble the bed frame before we can put the mattress on it.

children.definition: To take things out of the bag or box they were packed in.
children.example: Let's unpack the dishes first so we can eat at the table tonight.
children.translation_uz: buyumlarni quti yoki sumkadan olib chiqmoq
